items.title: Where German is spoken
items.claim: German is an official or co-official language of how many European countries?

options.text: Six (Germany, Austria, Switzerland, Liechtenstein, Luxembourg, Belgium)

items.reveal_title: Six European states give German official status
items.reveal:
It is the sole official language in Liechtenstein and one of multiple in Belgium (East Cantons), Luxembourg, Switzerland and Italy's South Tyrol.

German is the most widely spoken native language in the EU (around 95 million).
items.why: Language geography rarely matches state borders neatly.

items.title: East German vocabulary after 1990
items.claim: After German reunification (1990), East German specific vocabulary largely faded. One word that survived in widespread use is:
items.reveal_title: The Ampelmannchen survived as a cultural icon
items.reveal:
Created in 1961 by Karl Peglau, the East Berlin pedestrian-light figure was retained after unification following public campaigns.

Most specifically DDR-era political vocabulary disappeared from active use within a decade.
items.why: Symbols can outlive the political contexts that created them.

items.title: When the Grimms began publishing
items.claim: The first edition of the Brothers Grimm's Kinder- und Hausmarchen appeared in which year?
items.reveal:
Jacob and Wilhelm Grimm collected tales partly from middle-class informants of Huguenot background, including Dorothea Viehmann.

Later editions softened violence in some tales. Their later Deutsches Worterbuch project was completed only in 1961.
items.why: The 'folk' in folklore is often more bourgeois and literate than the framing implies.
